For the folk musician, see [[Johnny Flynn]].}} {{Infobox NCAA Athlete | name = | college = [[Syracuse University|Syracuse]] | sport = [[Basketball]] | position = [[Guard (basketball)|Guard]] | class = Sophomore | career_start = 2007 | jersey = 10 | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 0 | weight_lb = 186 | nationality = [[United States|American]] | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1989|2|6}} | birth_place = [[Niagara Falls, New York]] | highschool = [[Niagara Falls High School]] (N.Y.) }} '''Jonny Flynn''' (born February 6, 1989 in [[Niagara Falls, New York]]) is an [[United States|American]] [[college basketball]] player. The 6'0" (1.83 m) and 186 lbs. (84 kg) [[point guard]] plays for the [[Syracuse University|Syracuse]] [[Syracuse Orange|Orange]] and was widely considered one of the top point guards in college basketball.http://www.usatoday.com/sports/recruiting/basketball/national/2007-03-12-basketball.htmhttp://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Jonny-Flynn-1245/http://www.collegehoopsnet.com/college-basketball-top-point-guards-132930http://beyondthearc.msnbc.msn.com/archive/2008/10/14/1544916.aspx Flynn is also considered a top [[2009 NBA Draft]] point guard prospect.[http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2009/columns/story?columnist=ford_chad&page=FordDraftWatch-090115 Draft Watch: Getting to the point] ==High school== In the class of 2007, he was ranked as the No. 22 overall recruit and No. 4 point guard by Rivals.com and as the No. 23 overall and the No. 4 point guard by Scout.com and was a 2007 [[McDonald's All-American]]. He was named to the 2007 USA Basketball Junior National Select Team that will compete against the World Select Team in the 10th annual Nike Hoop Summit in Memphis, Tenn. He is a former high school teammate of current SU guard/forward [[Paul Harris (basketball)|Paul Harris]]. ==College== ===2007-08=== In his first ever game, on November 12, 2007, Flynn scored 28 points which eclipsed former Orange standout [[Carmelo Anthony]]'s record for most points in a freshman's debut.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=273160183 Freshman Flynn sets pace as Syracuse holds off Siena] A career-high, he matched his debut performance with another 28-point effort in an 82-77 loss to [[University of Pittsburgh|Pittsburgh]] on March 21, 2008.[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280610183 Pittsburgh snags fifth straight win at Syracuse] Flynn would go on to a prolific freshman year, collecting co-Big East Rookie of the Year honors with averages of 15.7 points and 5.3 assists per game. Flynn, along with fellow freshman [[Donte Greene]] were the second-highest scoring freshman duo in the country, combining to average 33.4 points per outing. ===2008-09=== Flynn was named to the preseason All Big East teamhttp://www.bigeast.org/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=19400&ATCLID=1605721 and started the season with a 27-point effort against [[Richmond University|Richmond]]http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=283230183 on November 18, 2008. Seven days later, Flynn scored 25 points and hit a 3-pointer with 6.4 seconds left in regulation as Syracuse defeated then-No. 23 ESPN/USA Today, No. 22 AP Kansas 89-81 in overtime in the championship game of the CBE Classic. Flynn was named MVP of the Tournament.http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283300183 Flynn's leaping ability was on display on a January 11, 2009 game against Rutgers. With Syracuse clinging to a 52-48 lead, Flynn drove to the hoop and threw down a monstrous dunk over 6-foot-3 Rutgers guard Michael Rosario as Rosario attempted to draw a charge.http://syracuse.scout.com/a.z?s=185&p=2&c=829345 http://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/index.ssf/2009/01/as_they_play_11_syracuse_vs_ru.htmlhttp://media.www.dailyorange.com/media/storage/paper522/news/2008/12/05/Sports/Mbb-GameChanger.Flynns.HighFlying.Dunk.Lifts.Syracuse.To.Win.Over.Rutgers-3583066.shtmlhttp://web.sny.tv/news/article.jsp?ymd=20090110&content_id=1487570&oid=2&vkey=21 In the quarterfinals of the 2009 [[Big East Tournament]] on March 12 and 13th, Flynn led the Orange to a 127-117 win in six overtimes over the favored [[University of Connecticut]] [[Huskies]]. Flynn played 67 minutes on the floor that evening, leading the Orange by scoring 34 points, adding 11 assists and making all 16 of his free throw attempts.http://espn.go.com/ncb/gamecast?gameId=290710041http://www.nytimes.com/2009/03/13/sports/ncaabasketball/13uconn.html?_r=1&hp Flynn then played all 45 minutes of Syracuse's 74-69 overtime victory over the [[West Virginia Mountaineers]] in the Big East semifinals. He scored 15 points and had 9 assists.http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/writers/kevin_armstrong/03/14/syracuse.wins.semifinal/index.html?eref=sircrc For his efforts, Flynn was named the 2009 Big East Tournament's MVP.http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/college/2009/03/14/2009-03-14_jonny_flynn_gets_big_east_mvp_nod.html In his first career NCAA tournament game in 2009, Flynn led all scorers in their first round matchup against Stephen F. Austin, tallying 16 points and 7 assists. Syracuse went on to win the game 59-44. On March 22nd, 2009 Flynn would score 11 points and add 7 assists as Syracuse defeated Arizona State 78-67 advancing Syracuse to its first Sweet Sixteen since 2004. http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=294000040 On April 9th, it was announced by Syracuse University that Flynn would declare himself eligible for the upcoming [[2009 NBA Draft]]. However, Flynn would retain is NCAA eligibility by not immediately hiring an agent. {{cite web|url=http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2009/04/syracuses_jonny_flynn_eric_dev.html|title=Syracuse's Jonny Flynn, Eric Devendorf and Paul Harris will enter the NBA draft|accessdate=2009-04-09|date=2009-04-09|first=Mike|last=Waters}} On April 13th, [[The Post-Standard]] reported that Flynn signed with agent Leon Rose, who also represents [[LeBron James]].{{cite web|url=http://blog.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/2009/04/syracuse_universitys_jonny_fly.html|title=Syracuse University's Jonny Flynn signs with agent, according to source|date=2009-04-13|accessdate=2009-04-13|first=Mike|last=Waters}} On April 15th, Flynn officially decided to forgo his final two years at Syracuse and signed with Creative Artists Agency Sports, run by agent Leon Rose. {{cite web|url=http://blog.syracuse.com/orange-segment/2009/04/interview_with_jonny_flynn_syr.html|title=Interview with Jonny Flynn: Syracuse basketball star officially signs an agent|first=Ryan|last=Miller|accessdate=2009-04-15|date=2009-04-15}} ==Team USA== Flynn was named as a 2006 USA Men's U18 National Team member on June 26, 2006 at the 2006 FIBA Americas U18 Championship for Men in [[San Antonio, Texas]]. During the tournament, he averaged 8.5 ppg., 3.8 rpg., a team-high 5.3 apg. and 1.8 spg.http://www.usabasketball.com/biosmen/johnny_flynn_bio.html Flynn would once again play on Team USA in the 2007 USA Basketball U19 World Championships. The team took home the silver medal, as Flynn averaged 9.6 ppg. in the USA's nine games.http://carrierdome.syr.edu/news/basketball/mbasket/2007/7/22/USA19U7.22.07.asp?path=mbasket?path=mbasket ==References== {{reflist|2}} ==External links== *[http://www.suathletics.com/roster.asp?playerid=2428&sport=176&roster=211&path=mbasket SUAthletics.com] {{start box}} {{s-ach}} {{succession box|title=[[NCAA Big East Basketball Rookie of the Year|NCAA Basketball
